summary:
[  edit  ]
NOTE
OS:  This operator is only supported under the  Microsoft Windows 10 April 2018 or newer  operating system.
The Kinect Azure  TOP  can be used to configure and capture data from a Microsoft Kinect Azure camera or a Kinect compatible  Orbbec  camera (Femto Mega, Femto Bolt, etc).
The  TOP  can be used to configure the settings of the camera (resolution, frame rate, synchronization, etc) as well to retrieve captured images from either its color or depth cameras. Image data from one camera can be remapped (aligned) to the other camera in order to match color and depth information. Only one Kinect Azure  TOP  can be connected to a single Kinect camera. To retrieve additional images from the same camera, use a  Kinect Azure Select TOP .
The Kinect Azure can also extract body tracking information and skeleton positions using the depth camera image. To access this data, use a  Kinect Azure CHOP  and set its Kinect  TOP  parameter to the primary  Kinect Azure TOP  that is connected to the device.  Note:  While both Microsoft and Orbbec hardware can be used in the same project, only one hardware type can have body tracking enabled at any one time. Body tracking is required for the Player Index image or to obtain skeleton data. If body tracking is not required from the Orbbec, it is recommended to use the native  Orbbec TOP  instead.
Note:  The Orbbec Femto Mega does not automatically support ethernet connections using the Kinect Azure  TOP  or  CHOP . However, you can enable detection of ethernet devices using an external configuration file places alongside your toe file. Ethernet connections only support depth and IR images, color video is only supported over USB. For further information on the file see the  Orbbec documentaion .
Warning:  When working with Orbbec hardware, using both Kinect Azure and Orbbec nodes in the same project may lead to instability. It is recommended to use either all Kinect Azure or all Orbbec nodes depending on project requirements.
TIP:  See Elburz' video on using KinectAzure's point clouds and a bunch of Azure general tips.  Kinect Azure Point Cloud in TouchDesigner Tutorial  on the Interactive and Immersive HQ.
See also  Kinect Azure CHOP ,  Kinect Azure Select TOP ,  Palette:pointRender ,  Palette:kinectCalibration ,  Palette:kinectRecorder ,  Palette:kinectPointcloud .

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Enable or disable the camera.  Note  Disabling this  TOP  will also disable any other operators ( Kinect Azure Select TOP  or  Kinect Azure CHOP ) that rely on it.

parameters.label: Hardware Type
parameters.name: library
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose whether you are using Microsoft Kinect Azure hardware or a Kinect compatible Orbbec camera (Femto Mega, Femto Bolt, etc). Both camera types can be used together in the same project, but only one hardware type can enable body tracking at any one time.

parameters.label: Microsoft Kinect Azure
parameters.name: microsoft
parameters.description: Select this option if you are using an original Microsoft Kinect Azure camera.

parameters.label: Orrbec Compatible (Femto Mega, Femto Bolt, ...)
parameters.name: orbbec
parameters.description: Selection this option for a Kinect compatible Orbbec camera e.g. Femto Mega, Femto Bolt, etc. Not all Orbbec cameras are compatible with the Kinect Azure. For general Orbbec support use an  Orbbec TOP .

parameters.label: Sensor
parameters.name: sensor
parameters.description: The serial number of the connected Kinect Azure camera. The  TOP  will automatically fill the list with all available cameras. Note: Only one Kinect Azure  TOP  should be connected to a single camera.

parameters.label: Camera  FPS
parameters.name: fps
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls the frame rate of both the color and depth cameras. Some higher camera resolutions are not supported when running at 30FPS. Lower framerates can produce brighter color images in low light conditions.

parameters.label: Color  Resolution
parameters.name: colorres
parameters.description: ⊞  - The resolution of images captured by the color camera. Different resolutions may have different aspect ratios. Note: 4096 x 3072 is not supported at 30  FPS .

parameters.label: 4096 x 3072 (4x3)
parameters.name: 4096x3072
parameters.description: Note: This resolution is not supported when operating at 30FPS. Reduce the framerate to 15 or 5  FPS  to use this setting.

parameters.label: Depth Mode
parameters.name: depthmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - The depth mode controls which of the Kinect's two depth cameras (Wide or Narrow FOV) are used to produce the depth image and whether any 'binning' is used to process the data. In 'binned' modes, 2x2 blocks of pixels are combined to produce a filter, lower resolution image. Note: Body tracking is not supported when using the Passive IR depth mode.

parameters.label: Narrow FOV
parameters.description: Unbinned (640x576)   narrowunbinned  -

parameters.label: Wide FOV
parameters.description: 2x2 Binned (512x512)   widebinned  -

parameters.label: Narrow FOV - 2x2 Binned (320x288)
parameters.name: narrowbinned
parameters.description: Note: This mode is not recommended for use with body tracking.

parameters.label: Wide FOV - Unbinned (1024x1024)
parameters.name: wideunbinned
parameters.description: Note: This mode is not supported at 30FPS and is not recommended for use with body tracking.

parameters.label: Passive IR (1024x1024)
parameters.name: passiveir
parameters.description: Note: This mode does not support body tracking.

parameters.label: Body Tracking Model
parameters.name: modelpath
parameters.description: The file path to the ONNX model that performs body tracking features. TouchDesigner includes the regular and lite models that are part of the Kinect Azure SDK.

parameters.label: Body Tracking Processing Mode
parameters.name: proccessingmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the body tracking model is processed. The default mode runs mostly on the  GPU  (supports Nvidia, AMD and Intel), but this can also be switched to a CPU mode when a compatible  GPU  is not available.

parameters.label: GPU  Default
parameters.name: gpudefault
parameters.description: The default processing mode. It is equivalent to DirectML when running on Windows.

parameters.label: CPU
parameters.name: cpu
parameters.description: The AI model will run on the CPU instead of the graphics cards. This is notably slower and not recommended for production release.

parameters.label: DirectML
parameters.name: directml
parameters.description: Equivalent to the default mode when running on Windows. The AI model will run on the  GPU . This is compatible with Nvidia, AMD and Intel GPUs.

parameters.label: Body Tracking  GPU  Device
parameters.name: gpu
parameters.description: The device number of the  GPU  to use when there are multiple GPUs in the system. The ordering system may be dependent on the  GPU  manufacturer.

parameters.label: Sensor Orientation
parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: ⊞  - Used to indicate when the camera is mounted in a non-upright position. This can help improve body-tracking results.

parameters.label: Image
parameters.name: image
parameters.description: ⊞  - A list of available image types to capture from the device and display in this  TOP . All image types have a second version that is mapped (aligned) to the image space of the other camera so that color and depth image data can be matched. The resolution of the image is controlled by the Color  Resolution  or Depth Mode parameters depending on the type of image selected. Use a  Kinect Azure Select TOP  to access additional image types from the same camera.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.name: color
parameters.description: An 8-bit RGBA image from the color camera.

parameters.label: Color aligned to Depth
parameters.name: colorremap
parameters.description: The color camera image remapped to align with the current depth camera image. The resolution is determined by the Depth Mode.

parameters.label: Depth
parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: A single channel 32bit floating point depth image where pixel values measure the distance in meters from the camera.  Resolution  and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode parameter.

parameters.label: Depth aligned to Color
parameters.name: depthremap
parameters.description: The depth image remapped to align with the current color camera image. The resolution is determined by the Color  Resolution  parameter.

parameters.label: IR
parameters.name: ir
parameters.description: A 16-bit integer infrared image captured by the depth camera.  Resolution  and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode.

parameters.label: IR aligned to Color
parameters.name: irremap
parameters.description: The infrared image remapped to align the current color camera image. The resolution is determined by the Color  Resolution  parameter.

parameters.label: Player Index
parameters.name: playerindex
parameters.description: An 8-bit single channel image that maps pixels to players that have been identified by the body tracking system. Pixel values represent the body id multiplied by 25 to improve contrast. Note: The player index map may have additional hardware requirements (CUDA capable graphics card) and may not synchronize with the color or depth images depending on current settings. The resolution is determined by the current Depth Mode.

parameters.label: Player Index aligned to Color
parameters.name: playerindexremap
parameters.description: The player index map remapped to align with the current color image. The resolution is determined by the Color  Resolution  parameter.

parameters.label: Point Cloud
parameters.name: pointcloud
parameters.description: A 32bit floating point RGBA image where the depth information has been converted into XYZ positions that are stored in the RGB channels. Position data is represented in meters and the resolution and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode. The Point Cloud image can be viewed in 3D by activating the  TOP  and selecting 'View as Points' in the right-click menu, or by using the  TOP  as an instance source in the Geometry  COMP .

parameters.label: Point Cloud aligned to Color
parameters.name: pointcloudremap
parameters.description: The point cloud image remapped to align with the current color image. Note: Remapping the image can create gaps and artifacts when view the points in 3D.

parameters.label: Align Image to Other Camera
parameters.name: remapimage
parameters.description: When enabled, the current image will be remapped to align with images from the other camera. For example, use this feature to create a color camera image that maps to the pixels of the depth camera.

parameters.label: Sync Image to Body Tracking
parameters.name: bodyimage
parameters.description: When enabled, the image produced will be delayed so that it corresponds to the most recent data in the body tracking system. The amount of delay may fluctuate based on the power of the processor doing the body tracking and the complexity of the scene. A  Kinect Azure Select TOP  can be used at the same time to retrieve the real-time image stream.

parameters.label: Mirror Image
parameters.name: mirrorimage
parameters.description: Flip the image in the horizontal axis.

parameters.label: CPU Body Tracking
parameters.name: cpu
parameters.description: When enabled, body tracking calculations will be done on the CPU rather than on the graphics card. This method is much slower, but does not require a high-powered graphics card to function.

parameters.label: Reset Color Controls
parameters.name: resetcolors
parameters.description: Reset all of the color controls to the camera's defaults. These vary per camera and may be different than the parameter defaults.

parameters.label: Enable Color Controls
parameters.name: enablecolors
parameters.description: Turn on to enable adjustment controls for the color camera. When disabled, the previous color settings will remain in place. Use the Reset Color Controls button to switch the camera back to its default settings.

parameters.label: Manual Exposure
parameters.name: manualexposure
parameters.description: Enable to allow setting the exposure time manually. When disabled, the camera will automatically choose an exposure based on the light levels and frame rate.

parameters.label: Exposure Time
parameters.name: exposure
parameters.description: Adjust the exposure time of the color image measured in microseconds. The time must be less than one frame.

parameters.label: Manual White Balance
parameters.name: manualwhitebalance
parameters.description: Enable to allow setting the camera white balance manually.

parameters.label: White Balance
parameters.name: whitebalance
parameters.description: Select the temperature in degrees Kelvin used to set the white balance of the image. The value is rounded to the nearest 10 degrees.

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.name: brightness
parameters.description: Used to adjust the brightness of the image from 0 to 255. 128 is the default.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.name: contrast
parameters.description: Conrtols the contrast of the color image.

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.name: saturation
parameters.description: Controls the saturation of the color image.

parameters.label: Sharpness
parameters.name: sharpness
parameters.description: Adjusts the sharpness of the color image.

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.name: gain
parameters.description: The gain of the color image.

parameters.label: Backlight Compensation
parameters.name: backlight
parameters.description: Enables compensation for bright back lighting in a scene.

parameters.label: Powerline Frequency
parameters.name: powerfreq
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the frequency of the power supply for use in the cameras noise cancellation system.

parameters.label: Depth Image Delay
parameters.name: depthdelay
parameters.description: A delay in microseconds between when the depth and color images are captured. The delay must be less than one frame in length based on the current framerate.

parameters.label: Wired Sync Mode
parameters.name: syncmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - When using more than one Kinect Azure camera, this setting can be used to determine which unit is the master and which are subordinates.

parameters.label: Subordinate Delay
parameters.name: subdelay
parameters.description: A delay in microseconds between when the master unit captures an image and when this device captures an image. (Only applicable for subordinate devices).

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Grow or shrink the input resolution to fit this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit the input resolution to be not larger than this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)

parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.
